health.summary: No signs of wear or failure.

findings.title: No signs of wear or failure
findings.detail: Every critical counter is at zero and the drive has logged no errors. Its self-tests passed.

findings.title: 5 sudden power losses
findings.detail: Each time the drive loses power while running, its heads park in an emergency. Unplugging without “Safely remove” is the usual cause, and it can leave weak sectors behind.

findings.title: Shingled (SMR) recording
findings.detail: A dense recording method that’s fine for backups and storage. Long continuous copies can slow down partway through.

indicators.label: S.M.A.R.T. verdict
indicators.help: The drive’s own overall pass/fail check.

indicators.label: Reallocated sectors
indicators.help: Damaged spots already replaced with spares. The most important wear sign.

indicators.label: Pending sectors
indicators.help: Sectors that read unreliably and are waiting to be re-tested.

indicators.label: Uncorrectable sectors
indicators.help: Sectors the drive couldn’t read during its own scan.

indicators.label: Drive error log
indicators.help: Read/write commands that failed.

indicators.label: Read error rate
indicators.help: Errors while reading data from the platters.

indicators.label: Seek error rate
indicators.help: Errors moving the read/write heads into position.

indicators.label: Spin retries
indicators.help: Times the motor needed a second try to reach full speed.

indicators.label: Interface CRC errors
indicators.help: Data damaged between drive and computer. Usually the cable or adapter.

indicators.label: Self-tests
indicators.help: Built-in diagnostics run by the drive. Aborted tests count as neither passed nor failed.

deductions.factor: Errors in the drive’s error log

health.summary: 1 sector can’t be read reliably. Everything else looks normal.

findings.title: 1 sector can’t be read reliably
findings.detail: The drive will re-test it the next time data is written there, then keep it if it was only a weak write, or swap in a spare if the surface is damaged. The drive logged 2 read errors on sector 66,572. Nothing has been replaced yet.
findings.action: Keep a backup of anything important, then run the drive’s extended self-test.

health.summary: Connected at USB 2.0 speed. Everything else looks normal.

findings.title: Connected at USB 2.0 speed
findings.detail: Windows shows this drive on a USB 2.0 (Hi-Speed) port (HS01), which limits it to about 40 MB/s. This isn’t a fault in the drive.
findings.action: Plug it straight into a USB 3 port (often blue or marked SS) using a USB 3 cable.
